title: A browser can request pairing that NOTHING can approve: moe up never prompts, censors a prompt, and drops the operator channel on a non-TTY launch
description:
FILED BY A FREE AGENT (yaron@cordum.io's standing "improve the UI so it is usable" mandate), 2026-08-27 at HEAD 52fda230, from a LIVE run of the shipped path: a real daemon hosting the built bundle, browser paired via playwright. Screens + full page dumps: C:/Users/Yaron/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--projexts-moe-next/267e8020-ee4d-4dc9-b5a4-46e4ed922380/scratchpad/shots (01-pairing, 17-after-reload); daemon transcript in .../scratchpad/lane/lane.log.

THE DEFECT, stated as the owner meets it. The first and only screen a new operator sees says: "Type this exact label into the foreground terminal that launched this project." Four measured facts make that instruction unfollowable:

(1) THE TERMINAL NEVER ASKS. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-main.ts announce() (~:227-240) prints exactly three lines: "moe up: daemon listening on <origin>", "moe up: control room -> open <origin> (hosted by the daemon from <root>)", "moe up: ctrl-c here stops both children". Nothing says a code will appear in the browser or that it must be typed back. When the browser creates the request the only new terminal line is the access log "POST /session/pair/request" (http-listener.ts:701). Confirmed in lane.log: no prompt around that line.

(2) THE LAUNCHER WOULD CENSOR A PROMPT IF ONE EXISTED. moe-up-main.ts:37 SENSITIVE_DAEMON_LINE matches /confirmation[-_ ]?label/iu and :49-52 suppresses any daemon line matching it. A daemon-side prompt containing the phrase "confirmation label" is swallowed by the launcher before the operator sees it. Any fix must change BOTH sides or the new prompt is invisible.

(3) TYPING PRODUCES NO ECHO, RIGHT OR WRONG. daemon-main.ts:169-175 calls started.approvePairing(line) and DISCARDS the result: approved, PAIRING_CONFIRMATION_UNKNOWN and PAIRING_REQUEST_EXPIRED are all silent. Any line failing /^[0-9a-f]{4}(?:-[0-9a-f]{4}){2}$/u (uppercase, trailing space, the INSTANCE-prefixed form the browser itself instructs) is dropped unannounced at moe-up-main.ts:285 and daemon-main.ts:171. Contrast project-manager-main.ts:303-311, which DOES disclose its refusals - the manager already has the behaviour this path lacks.

(4) A NON-TTY LAUNCH SILENTLY HAS NO OPERATOR CHANNEL AT ALL. moe-up-main.ts:350 passes operatorInput only when process.stdin.isTTY === true; without it :201 omits --operator-stdin, so daemon-main.ts:195-197 has no operator channel. POST /session/pair/request still succeeds and the browser still renders a code (pairing-approval-handshake.ts:161-168). An IDE run window, a piped launch, or a service start therefore shows the operator a code that NOTHING in the running system can ever approve, with no statement to that effect anywhere. THIS IS THE UNUSABLE-PRODUCT CASE and it fails closed only in the sense that nobody gets in.

WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A COMMENT (board filing bar): it is a correctness defect REACHABLE ON THE SHIPPED PATH TODAY - `pnpm start` is the documented entry, and case (4) makes the product unusable with no diagnosis. Every pairing row (task-959df79d, task-164fdb12, task-527bab5d, task-c46017f6) is DONE, so no open row owns it.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (the architect owns the real plan):
- The daemon, when a pairing request is created, prints ONE operator line that survives the launcher filter, e.g. "A browser wants to pair. Type the code it shows here, then press Enter." Choose wording that does not collide with SENSITIVE_DAEMON_LINE, or narrow that regex so a prompt with no secret in it passes (the CODE ITSELF must still never be printed by the daemon - it lives only in the browser; that rail stays).
- After each typed line the daemon prints the outcome in plain words: "Paired." / "That code is not one Moe is waiting for." / "That code expired - reload the browser page for a new one.", with code@layer after it, mirroring project-manager-main.ts.
- POST /session/pair/request answers an `operatorChannel: boolean` the daemon already knows (options.operatorInput !== undefined) so the browser can replace the type-this-code instruction with the honest "Moe was started without a terminal it can listen on; stop it and run it again from a terminal window" instead of showing an unapprovable code. This is a daemon-STATED fact, not a UI-invented one.
- Accept the label case-insensitively and trimmed at both filters, since the browser renders it in a font where case is not obvious.

NOT IN SCOPE: making the session survive a page reload (separate policy question - the credential is deliberately memory-only), and the control room's silent no-op after pressing "I entered this label" while the claim is refused (that needs live-handshake.ts to carry the refusal code up; file separately or fold in, architect's call).
definitionOfDone: `pnpm start` on an interactive terminal prints, when and only when a browser has requested pairing, a prompt that names what the operator must type; proven by a test that drives the real launcher line filter (not just the daemon) and asserts the prompt is NOT suppressed by SENSITIVE_DAEMON_LINE.

Every typed operator line produces one plain-language outcome line for approved, unknown-code and expired-request, each with its code@layer; drilled by deleting the disclosure and observing the arm red.

A non-TTY launch either establishes an operator channel or the browser is told, from a daemon-stated fact carried on the pair/request response, that no terminal can approve it - proven end to end with stdin not a TTY, asserting the browser-visible sentence and asserting NO unapprovable code is presented as actionable.
The pairing code itself still never appears in daemon stdout, launcher stdout, argv, or any URL; the existing secrecy arms stay green and one of them is drilled.
Case- and whitespace-tolerant acceptance of the typed label at both the launcher and daemon filters, with a hostile arm for an uppercase and a trailing-space spelling.
taskRails: The code is authored by the daemon and shown only in the browser. Nothing in this task may print, log or pass the code through the terminal, argv or a URL.
Any operator-facing sentence must be a fact the daemon knows, never a UI guess.
moe-up-main.ts and daemon-main.ts both carry filters; a change to one without the other is a no-op in production. Prove the whole chain, not one half.

implementationPlan.note:
Three named frozen rosters, each wired so a deleted member REDS a count rather than shrinking its own iteration silently.

OPERATOR_OUTCOME_LINES — restructured this step. My first draft indexed it by hand ([0]/[1]/[2]) and merely pushed keys, which is the roster-shaped defect the global rail names: deletion would have been a tsc error, not an executed-count red. J2 now ITERATES the roster and dispatches through a `drivers` map keyed by plain `string` (deliberately NOT by the roster's own union, so a member with no driver fails loudly at runtime instead of type-checking itself out of existence). The roster is listed in EXECUTION order (UNKNOWN, APPROVED, EXPIRED) because the arms are order-dependent — APPROVED consumes the live request and EXPIRED needs a fresh one plus the 63s wait. Asserted: executed.length === OPERATOR_OUTCOME_LINES.length, executed key-set === roster key-set, and a pinned toHaveLength(3).

HOSTILE_SPELLINGS — exact count 2 (UPPERCASE, TRAILING_SPACE), swept across BOTH filters inside the UNKNOWN driver, so the executed case count is HOSTILE_SPELLINGS.length * 2 = 4 and is asserted against the roster length, not a literal 4. Each iteration asserts the outcome-line COUNT reached `seen`, so a dropped spelling cannot hide behind a previous arm's line.

SECRECY_SURFACES — exact count 6 (daemon-stdout, daemon-stderr, launcher-log, daemon-argv, observed-urls, j1-page-dom). J3 asserts set-EQUALITY between the swept keys and the roster (both directions, so an unswept surface is a red, not a silent skip) plus a pinned toHaveLength(6), and requires each surface to be non-empty before testing it — an empty string would pass every `not.toContain` vacuously.

Verified green after the restructure: `npx playwright test -c tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts --grep "J1:|J2:|J3:"` -> 3 passed (1.2m), EXIT=0; `tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json` EXIT=0. File 435 lines.
